title: Exchange Destination
text: Year 3 means exchange, no exceptions. The international office opens the list: four continents, one university each. Some are a train ride away, some a long-haul flight. Somewhere out there, a dorm room and a new version of you are waiting.

hints: Every continent is an adventure: never say a destination is bad.
The trip footprint is shown on each card; you may nod to the train-versus-plane contrast without lecturing.

title: Life in {city}
text: You've landed in {city}. Your stories already feature a skyline, a street-food stall and a suspiciously aesthetic coffee. Classmates are planning weekends everywhere. How much do you move?

ai.tone: wide-eyed, sensory, specific to the city
hints: The flight option is fun; never shame it, just let the numbers speak later.

effects.text: You find the best cheap noodle place in {city} and become a regular. That's a kind of passport too.

footprint.label: Trains and buses during the exchange

effects.text: Nine-hour bus rides, one stolen sandwich, zero regrets.
Twelve countries, twelve stories, one very tired passport.

title: The Research Paper
text: The summer after the exchange belongs to the mandatory research paper: forty pages, one supervisor, zero excuses. ChatGBT is open in another tab, blinking at you like a slot machine. How do you use it?

hints: This choice decides how the player's skills hold up when AI gets much stronger at 38–40.
Do not reveal that consequence explicitly; hint at 'what you'll actually know'.

effects.text: The paper writes itself in a week. You're not entirely sure what it says.

choices.label: Targeted: a few prompts a day
choices.hint: A sparring partner, not a ghostwriter

effects.text: You argue with the model, win twice, lose once, and learn more than either of you.
Your supervisor writes 'finally, a human voice' in the margin.

title: The Six-Month Internship
text: Year 4, back from the exchange. The six-month internship is where job offers are born: your inbox holds three recruiter emails and one suspicious 'opportunity'. Whatever you pick will probably become your first job, so pick like it matters.

hints: Reference the summer internship and the asso when explaining what's unlocked.
Most internships end with a return-offer test (a skill check): passing it opens prestigious employers at the first-job step.
Locked options show their reason; say which past choice would have opened them.

choices.label: Big Tech AI product team
choices.lockedReason: Requires an AI or startup asso, or a startup internship

effects.text: Your A/B test ships to forty million people. Your mum asks if you 'fixed the internet'.

success.text: Return-offer coding interview: your Math & AI carried you. You reverse the binary tree, then explain why nobody should ever have to.

failure.text: Return-offer coding interview: Math & AI check failed. An off-by-one error, live, with the interviewer gently nodding. You'll dream of it.

choices.label: Bank or asset manager
choices.lockedReason: Requires a finance club or a bank internship

effects.text: Your model values a company at 2.3 billion. Your rent is still due on the 5th.

success.text: Return-offer quant test: Intelligence and Math & AI carried you. You price the dice game in your head and they stop the clock early.

failure.text: Return-offer quant test failed: the dice game had three dice, not two. You notice on the train home.

effects.text: You learn that 'let's take this offline' means 'never'. Also, how to align a text box to the pixel.

success.text: Return-offer case interview: your Economics and Charisma carried you. 'How many croissants are sold in Paris a day?' You nailed it, and the partner smiled.

failure.text: Return-offer case interview: your Economics wobbled on the market sizing. You estimated more croissants than people on Earth.

choices.label: Research lab: ML, health, econ
choices.lockedReason: Requires a lab internship or Math & AI ≥ 55

effects.text: You co-author your first paper. Your name is sixth of seven. You print it anyway.

choices.label: International AI or climate policy
choices.lockedReason: Requires an AI asso or an impact background

effects.text: You take the night train to Geneva and spend six months drafting paragraph 14(b). It matters, eventually.

success.text: Final panel: your Intelligence and Charisma carried you. A grey-haired diplomat writes 'sharp' on a napkin.

failure.text: Final panel: you blank on the question about the precautionary principle. The panel is very polite about it, which is worse.

choices.label: NGO
choices.lockedReason: Requires the Impact asso or an NGO internship

effects.text: Your project gets three thousand families connected to clean water data. Your salary is a thank-you card.
You present to an executive committee. Someone says 'interesting' and you replay it for a week.

success.text: Final case presentation: your Economics and Charisma carried you. The executive committee asks for your slides. The real ones, not the backup.

failure.text: Final case presentation: your Economics wobbled on the market sizing. Someone says 'interesting' again, but differently.
